documents.description: User mandate 2026-07-09: serious UI polish on Studio and the Desk Structure; fix bad design mistakes; make the new theme system visibly hit everywhere. STRUCTURE DOCTRINE: (1) the main Desk Structure is CLEAN — what matters first: Papers, Sheets, Tasks; (2) a 'Plugins' slot in Structure holds plugin-owned trees (Onix, Tickets, Lightning Storm/pulse, ...) UNLESS a per-plugin setting promotes it into the main structure; (3) Media is reachable via the top-menu Media surface, so it is hidden from Structure by default (visible by setting); (4) whatever finds no place under the main slots or Plugins lands in a '...Rest' folder — the tree must still tell the TRUTH about the database, nothing silently invisible; (5) plugins can be DISABLED even though installed, and some plugins are OFF by default — workspaces should be clean in general. Charter: .claude/workflows/bp-studio-structure-polish-charter.md

purpose.why: The larger Studio + Structure Polish — make every workspace open to a calm, truthful, theme-coherent desk with explicit plugin placement. mixed core and plugin trees, hid some database content, applied theme inconsistently, and initially bound Workspace Settings too loosely to scope. Introducing tiered structure, per-workspace enablement and placement, an honest Rest census, scoped settings guards, and visual/token verification was the right intervention because the server-owned structure tree is shared by Studio and TUI, so fixing ownership and scope once keeps both consumers truthful. If omitted, users see a noisy or misleading desk and can accidentally edit settings for a workspace other than the one shown.
